title: Briefing: Canada, India, South Africa, Italy, Albania and France
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Saturday, October thirty-first. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means only one source has it so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.
Canada. APTN News reports: "Feds declare Roberts Bank 2 expansion ‘project of national interest’". Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, APTN News, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

India. CJP president Abhijeet Dipke posted an Instagram note explaining his earlier criticism of singer Diljit Dosanjh and urging him to end the dispute. We grade that reported: one source so far, not yet independently confirmed.
South Africa. IOL reports: "Cars torched, shops shut as asylum ruling fuels fresh unrest in Soweto and Durban". Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, IOL, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

Italy. Farmers and truckers have blocked highways and ports in southern Italy to protest rising fuel prices, NBC News reports. We grade that reported: one source so far, not yet independently confirmed.

Albania. Albania's government has presented its 2027 tax package, dropping an earlier plan to raise corporate income tax, cutting VAT on 54 basic foods from 20% to 6% while raising the standard rate to 21%. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Tirana Times, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

France. The interior ministry says 410,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday, including 110,000 in Paris, in marches over the cost of living and the high-school movement; the CGT union puts both figures at nearly double the official count. We grade that reported: so far only Al Jazeera has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.

Canada's Pacific Link pipeline fight. Imperial Oil's chief executive said he is encouraged by progress toward a binding Pathways carbon-storage agreement with Ottawa and Alberta, a condition for the Pacific Link pipeline, though "there's still a lot of work left to do," BNN Bloomberg reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, BNN Bloomberg, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

The Cockroach Janta Party movement. CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke attended Diljit Dosanjh’s concert in Delhi and posted an Instagram selfie and open letter expressing admiration despite a prior dispute, News18 reports. We grade that reported: one source so far, not yet independently confirmed. The Madras High Court has issued notices, returnable in six weeks, to the Union government, law-enforcement agencies and CJP spokesperson Saurav Das on a public-interest petition seeking a probe into his identity and nationality, News18 reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, News18, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.
South Africa's asylum ruling unrest. Coming up: local government elections on November fourth.

Italy's student and cost-of-living protests. Tens of thousands marched in Rome, Milan and other Italian cities on Friday against the cost of living and military spending, NBC News reports, as the USB union and others called public- and private-sector strikes. We grade that reported: so far only NBC News has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation. A Milan judge orders the release of the alleged administrator of the Movimento 17 Ottobre Telegram group, held since October twenty-fourth on suspicion of incitement, saying there are no serious grounds to believe he committed the offences; Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni calls the decision "shameful", Reuters reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Reuters, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

Albania's student protests. Tirana’s Chamber of Commerce and Industry and Pro Export Albania oppose the government’s proposed 2027 fiscal package, which the Albanian Daily News says would raise dividend tax from 8% to 15% and tourism VAT from 6% to 10%; it also cites a corporate income tax rise to 17%, which Tirana Times reports was dropped before the package was formally presented on October twenty-eighth. We grade that reported: so far only Albanian Daily News has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation. The Guardian reports that Albania's government adopted legislative measures imposing fines of up to 500,000 leks for individuals who remain in a crowd where violence, looting, or identity concealment occurs. Our grade: reported, from a single source so far.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
